videos.script: The shop has a network for production and one for staging. Both need the office, a firewall and the same DNS. {{two}} Building those things twice would double the bill and the mistakes. So they go in one network, the hub. {{hub}} Each workload's network is a spoke, joined to the hub by a peering. {{peering}} A peering is two links, one on each side. It works only when both exist. {{sides}} And the two address ranges must not overlap. One shared address, and the peering is refused. {{overlap}} Now the surprise. Production is peered to the hub. Staging is peered to the hub. Production still cannot reach staging. {{transitive}} A peering passes nothing on. To cross from one spoke to another, a packet has to go through a device in the hub. {{firewall}} For the shop, that is exactly right. The only road between its environments runs through a firewall, where it is written down. {{end}}
